title: Ledger Engine
tagline: Build a double-entry ledger that refuses to go out of balance, then reconcile it against a bank statement.
summary: An in-memory double-entry ledger: exact integer money, a chart of accounts with normal balance sides, an append-only journal that rejects unbalanced or mixed-currency entries, balances and a trial balance derived from the journal, reversals, and a two-pass reconciliation that reports every break with totals that tie out.
youWillBuild: A ledger engine that posts balanced journal entries, derives balances and a zero-sum trial balance, reverses mistakes, and reconciles a bank account against an external statement.

languageWhy.Java: Records and sealed-ish exception hierarchies make the value types and the 'ledger said no' contract explicit; Math.addExact shows what overflow-safe money looks like.
languageWhy.Python: Frozen dataclasses and enums give the same value types with far less ceremony; because Python ints never overflow, the port keeps an explicit 64-bit bound so you see what Math.addExact was protecting.

skills: Represent money as integer minor units with explicit rounding and lossless allocation
Model a chart of accounts with account types and normal balance direction
Post immutable journal entries that balance per currency and carry ids and sequence numbers
Derive signed balances, point-in-time balances, and a trial balance that sums to zero
Reconcile ledger postings against an external statement and report breaks that tie out

prerequisites.title: Representing Money: Minor Units, Currencies, and Rounding
Reconciliation: Matching Your Ledger Against Theirs

stages.title: Money and the Chart of Accounts
stages.summary: Exact Money arithmetic (parse, plus, minus, times with rounding, allocate) and an account registry where every account type knows which side it grows on.

stages.title: Balanced Journal Entries
stages.summary: An append-only journal that accepts an entry only if its debits equal its credits in one currency, assigns sequence numbers, and de-duplicates on entry id.

stages.title: Balances, Trial Balance, and Reversals
stages.summary: Derive signed balances from the journal (with periodic snapshots), read a balance as of any sequence number, produce a trial balance whose columns agree, and reverse entries by mirroring them.

stages.title: Reconcile Against a Statement
stages.summary: Match a bank or processor account's ledger lines against an external statement by reference, then by amount within a date window, and report every break by category with totals that tie out.
